reasoning.text: The render reads convincingly as an FPGA NTT accelerator floorplan, but the exploded finned heatsink is oversized and centred over the +X control region, so in the TOP plan view it occludes the twiddle ROM, address-generation unit and schedule/FSM controller — the worst remaining X-ray failure. The shared Barrett reduction spine (mod_red_mult/subshift) is also partly hidden behind the +X pipeline-register column in ISO. Everything else (open array frame, 8 distinct banks/lanes, layered+arrowed dataflow buses, exploded radix-4 cutaway) is faithful and legible.
gaps: The shared Barrett reduction spine (mod_red_mult cylinder + mod_red_subshift) is partly occluded by the +X pipeline-register column in ISO; consider nudging the register column -X or raising the reduction spine slightly so both reduction members read in the X-ray.

Source-missing structures remain committed placeholders (conflict-free Sec.III bank()/offset() map, per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s, rearranged-loop twiddle-ROM addressing f(stage,block), exact FSM transition table) — the PDF body is FlateDecode-undecodable, so these cannot be made paper-faithful until the paper text is gathered; they are correctly labelled [conv]/[source-missing] and out of scope for the functional axis.

The committed twiddle ROM still embeds a bit-reversed index, which is in tension with the headline natural-order/no-bit-reversal datapath claim; resolving this needs the paper's rearranged-loop addressing.

fields.before: EXPLODED ABOVE: the aluminum finned heatsink that clamps onto the FPGA package lid over the whole die, lifted high on a riser stub so it floats clearly above the datapath and the Barrett reduction spine — keeping the die floorplan and the +X pipeline-register column visible in the ISO X-ray rather than swallowing them. Ten 0.12 m fins at 0.3 m pitch over a 3x4 m baseplate, modeled as ONE finned block (the fin comb is decoration captured in spec, not ten separate parts).
fields.after: EXPLODED ABOVE: the aluminum finned heatsink (the package thermal lid) that clamps onto the FPGA package over the +X control/reduction region of the die, lifted high on a riser stub so it floats clearly above the datapath and the Barrett reduction spine. Its footprint was shrunk (z-extent -1.3..1.3) so the twiddle ROM (z=-2.5), address-generation (z=+2.5) and schedule blocks below stay visible in the ISO X-ray and the TOP plan view rather than being swallowed. Eight 0.12 m fins at 0.3 m pitch over a 2.4x2.6 m baseplate, modeled as ONE finned block (the fin comb is decoration captured in spec, not eight separate parts).

before.notes: Consolidated finned heatsink — the prior ten heatsink_fin_* parts were pure decoration and have been collapsed into this single block with the fin geometry recorded in params (anti-decoration rule).

after.notes: Consolidated finned heatsink — the prior ten heatsink_fin_* parts were pure decoration and were collapsed into this single block with the fin geometry recorded in params (anti-decoration rule). Footprint reduced and raised this pass so it no longer blankets the +X control cluster in plan view; it represents the exploded package thermal lid, not full-die coverage.

fields.before: Support stub grounding the exploded heatsink baseplate down to the silicon die, showing where the heatsink seats on the package in the assembled machine; lengthened so the baseplate floats well clear of the datapath.
fields.after: Support stub grounding the exploded heatsink baseplate down to the silicon die, showing where the heatsink seats on the package in the assembled machine; lengthened so the baseplate floats well clear of the datapath and control cluster.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic, then scribe three thin floorplan partition lines dividing the die into memory, butterfly-array and reduction/control zones; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view; add two +X dataflow arrows (mult->add/sub, add/sub->register) on the exploded unit and a thin carbon-fiber fusion-callout strut from the lanes-6/7 yoke up to the exploded baseplate so the W1->W2->W3->j-rotator->add/sub->register order and the represented fused unit are unambiguous, and clamp the finned aluminum heatsink high onto its riser stub well above the die so the datapath below stays visible.
